equity_bridge.item: Dividends paid since the 2025-10-31 balance sheet (4 x $0.30 x ~55.0m shares, Nov-25/Feb-26/May-26/Aug-26)
equity_bridge.note: Estimate; FY2025 cash dividends were $61.8m (ENGH.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:1671) at a mix of $0.26 and $0.30 quarterly rates. The FY2026 flows are credited in year 1 but the cash already distributed out of them is not in the Oct-2025 cash balance. Replace with the actual balance sheet once the FY2026 filings are extracted.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR (FY2025 -> FY2035, forward), not a historical CAGR: every historical window is either flattered by acquisitions and FX (revenue 3-yr +5.3%) or depressed by the FY2020 Vidyo/COVID peak (5-yr), and the organic trajectory entering FY2026 is -6% to -8%. Equity CAGR was rejected as the growth source because 3-yr equity +6.2% diverges from 3-yr EPS -7.6% by far more than 30%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR +6.2% vs EPS 3-yr CAGR -7.6% and owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR -1.9%: book value is growing through retained earnings while per-share earnings and owner cash flow shrink. The 5-yr equity CAGR (+4.2%) is additionally depressed by the Feb-2021 C$1.50/share special dividend (~$83m of the $115.7m FY2021 dividends paid).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less interest income, CAD m): FY2020 162.1, FY2021 112.9, FY2022 99.4, FY2023 106.3, FY2024 118.8, FY2025 93.8. The owner-FCF CAGRs sit below the reported ones over both windows (3-yr -1.9% vs +0.3%; 5-yr -10.4% vs -9.0%) because interest income grew from $0.7m to $8-10m as rates rose on a ~$270m cash pile -- an increasing share of reported FCF is interest on cash, not operations. SBC is immaterial (0.2-0.5% of revenue) and is not the driver of the gap. All windows are post the Jan-2019 2-for-1 split (FY2018 EPS 2.11 is pre-split, 1.055 adjusted) so no per-share figure needed restating; FY2024 revenue growth (+10.7%) was itself mostly the Lifesize/Mediasite/SeaChange acquisitions and FX, with constant-currency organic revenue already shrinking.

scenario_narratives.base: Enghouse is a no-growth cash generator, not a compounder. The ~70% recurring base keeps shrinking organically at a moderating rate (-4% to -5% in FY2026-27 constant currency, easing to -2% by FY2029) while ~$30m/yr of debt-free tuck-ins -- the Aculab/Margento/Trafi/Sixbell pattern -- fill most of the hole; reported revenue bottoms around $450m in FY2028-29 and grows 2% nominal thereafter. The axes are (1) whether churn in the Lifesize and legacy on-premise bases moderates once the acquired cohorts have reset, (2) whether $2-2.5m/quarter of restructuring savings hold the margin at 25% against deleverage, and (3) whether the acquisition pipeline keeps delivering at ~1-1.5x revenue. Margins settle at management's 'mid-20s', not the high-20s of FY2023-24. Acquisition spend is charged as capex so the growth is paid for.
scenario_narratives.bull: Demand stabilises in FY2027 as enterprise IT budgets reopen and tariff uncertainty fades; the AMG segment (transit e-ticketing/MaaS, 5G OSS/BSS, public safety) keeps growing double digits and comes to dominate the mix; Enghouse uses its ~$270m of cash and the down-cycle in small-software valuations to buy more, cheaper, converting 7.5% of revenue of M&A into 3-3.5% net growth. Restructuring plus a higher-margin mix lifts adjusted EBITDA to 27%. Margin recovery, demand stabilisation and accretive M&A all have to happen together, which is why this case carries the lowest weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI-native contact-centre entrants and the hyperscalers (Amazon Connect, Microsoft, NICE, Genesys, Five9) take the renewals Enghouse's legacy and acquired customers would otherwise have signed; organic decline runs -5% to -7% and recurring revenue, the core of the thesis, keeps falling as it did in FY2025 and the first nine months of FY2026. Tuck-ins continue but buy shrinking assets, so the net top line is still falling in FY2035; fixed costs and leases delever and the margin holds at 22% only through repeated restructuring charges. The disciplined-compounder premium is gone and the stock is a melting ice cube with a dividend. The balance sheet means this is a value, not a survival, question.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Enghouse as what it is now -- a debt-free, ~25%-margin software business whose organic revenue is shrinking and whose growth is bought with cash -- rather than as the acquisition compounder of FY2013-2020. Three choices carry the valuation: acquisitions are treated as capex so the revenue path is paid for; the EBITDA margin anchors on management's own 'mid-20s' guidance after restructuring charges, not the FY2023-24 peak; and the probability weights lean to the bear because the decline is already in the reported numbers. The ~$270m cash pile is added once (interest income is stripped from the flows) and reduced for the dividends paid since the stale October-2025 balance sheet. Leases are charged as an operating cost and excluded from net debt. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, at a single CAD-built 8.5% cost of equity.
key_risks_to_valuation: The organic decline does not moderate: the base case assumes constant-currency churn eases from ~-5% to ~-2% by FY2029; if FY2026's pace persists the bear case is the base case
Acquisition capex productivity: the base assumes ~6% of revenue buys ~4% of revenue growth at ~1-1.5x sales; dearer deals or integration churn (the Lifesize pattern) mean the same cash buys less
Margin: 'mid-20s' after recurring restructuring charges may prove optimistic if restructuring becomes a permanent annual cost -- FY2025 $5.1m, Q3 FY2026 $4.6m
Stale anchors: cash, share count and the dividends-paid bridge are estimates from the 2025-10-31 balance sheet; the Q1-Q3 FY2026 interims were not extracted
FX: 85-90% of revenue is non-CAD and unhedged; a stronger CAD lowers reported revenue, margin and the CAD value of foreign cash
Capital allocation change: management has flagged that a larger deal could be debt- or equity-funded, which would break the flat-count, debt-free model
Key-person: Chairman/CEO Stephen Sadler is the acquisition engine; no succession is disclosed

data_sources.financials: ENGH.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt (audited consolidated statements, year ended 2025-10-31: income statement lines 1555-1595, cash flow 1638-1680, equity statement 1602-1628, tax note 2739-2752, EPS note 2858-2889, lease note 3002-3014); ENGH.TO_Metrics.csv / metrics_normalized history FY2013-FY2025; Q3 FY2026 figures (2026-09-10 release) as summarised in ENGH.TO_Analysis.json -- not in the Extracted folder

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, consolidated statement of cash flows 'Stock-based compensation expense' 1,324 (thousands; ENGH.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:1651); cross-checked to the equity statement 'Value of services recognized' 1,324 (line 1611). No cash taxes on net-share settlement are disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 in every period) so the combined figure equals the add-back.
inputs.share_count_basis: 54,754,683 common shares outstanding at 2025-10-31 (equity statement, ENGH.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:1614) plus ~2k dilutive options (diluted WA 55,153k vs basic 55,151k, note 12 line 2887) = 54.76m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. The count is a repurchaser's flat count -- NCIB bought 619,518 shares for $14.7m in FY2025 and buybacks continued into FY2026, so the true count at July 2026 is somewhat lower (conservative direction). Post-split basis: the Jan-2019 2-for-1 split doubled the count from 27.3m to 54.6m; every CAGR window below starts at FY2020 or later so no split adjustment is needed, and FY2013-FY2018 per-share figures in the Metrics CSV are pre-split.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CAD, the currency of the flows: Government of Canada 10-year ~3.4%, equity risk premium ~5.1%, beta 1.0 (ENGH's observed beta is ~0.8-0.9 but it is a ~C$900m-cap stock whose organic revenue is shrinking; rounding up to 1.0 costs ~0.6pp). Cost of equity 8.5%; no debt, so WACC = cost of equity = 8.5%. The same rate is used in all three scenarios -- cyclicality, churn and M&A-execution risk are charged ONCE, in the scenario flows and weights, not again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: the full IFRS-16 lease cash payment (FY2025 $6,074k = principal $5,569k + interest $505k, note 14 'Payments, including repayments of interest', ENGH.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:3010) is charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path (1.2% of revenue), and lease liabilities ($11,141k at 2025-10-31) are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for the cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation (depreciation $2,518k + amortisation of acquired intangibles $29,492k = $32,010k, 6.4% of FY2025 revenue) so the lease is not charged twice. The EBITDA margin path is therefore the company's post-IFRS-16 adjusted EBITDA, stated AFTER special/restructuring charges (results from operating activities + depreciation + ROU depreciation = $122,516k, 24.6% -- the Metrics CSV 'ebitda' line) and before SBC (+$1,324k -> 24.8%), with the lease charge taken separately below it.
inputs.nci_treatment: None required: no non-controlling interests (net income is 100% attributable; equity statement has no NCI column).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, enterprise software; net cash, real earnings, no REIT/bank/LIC characteristics). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. Non-US adaptations applied: CAD-built WACC, single lease treatment (B), interest income stripped with the cash pile in the bridge, SBC kept explicit at 0.3%. ACQUISITIONS ARE CAPEX: Enghouse's growth is bought, not organic -- PP&E capex is 0.3% of revenue but acquisitions ran $33.4m (FY2025) and $43.4m (FY2024). Every scenario's revenue path assumes continued tuck-in M&A, so capex_pct_path carries ~6% of revenue of acquisition spend (base) on top of 0.35% PP&E; projecting bought growth without charging for it would be the serial-acquirer version of the free-growth error. The matching D&A path glides from 6.3% to 4.0% as the large Vidyo/Dialogic-era intangibles finish amortising and are replaced by amortisation on the smaller ongoing deal flow, so the acquired-intangibles tax shield is not perpetuated at the FY2025 level. ANCHOR VINTAGE: the latest extracted filing is the FY2025 annual (balance sheet 2025-10-31). Q1-Q3 FY2026 interim reports exist (the Q3 FY2026 release of 2026-09-10 is summarised in the Analysis JSON: revenue $117.6m vs $125.6m, nine-month $352.0m vs $374.4m, recurring $81.7m vs $87.8m, net income $15.4m vs $17.2m, $4.6m further restructuring) but were not extracted, so cash and share count are eleven months old. Because FY2026 is modelled as forecast year 1 from the FY2025 base, the FY2026 cash generation is inside the flows but the dividends paid out of it since the balance-sheet date are not -- they are deducted in equity_bridge (four quarterly payments of $0.30 on ~55m shares, ~$66m, an estimate to be replaced by the actual July-2026 / October-2026 balance sheet). Buybacks since the balance-sheet date are value-neutral at the flat count and are ignored. The Sixbell telco acquisition (closed Nov 2025, price undisclosed in the extracted filings) is covered by year-1 acquisition capex. FX: ~85-90% of revenue is non-CAD with no hedging; CAD strength in 2026 is a reported-revenue headwind that is inside the year-1 growth figure and not modelled separately. Street basis: SBC is only 0.27% of revenue so the house/street band is a few cents wide and band_position is not meaningful -- read the house value. Cash-tax rate 20% in base: book ETR 19.5% (FY2025) / 19.7% (FY2024) against a 26.5% Canadian statutory rate, with tax-exempt income and lower foreign rates offset by dividend-repatriation withholding; cash taxes paid ran 80-100% of the provision over FY2021-25. 21% in bear (less tax-exempt income, withholding leakage persists), 20% in bull.
inputs.owner_fcf_fy2025_fully_loaded_note: On the model's own fully-loaded definition (owner FCF less the $5.6m lease principal and $33.4m of acquisitions) FY2025 owner FCF was ~$54.8m, not $93.8m: the house last_fcf keeps the contract definition (reported FCF less SBC less interest income) and the lease and acquisition charges enter through lease_cost_pct_path and capex_pct_path.

bear.rationale: The IMG contact-centre/video core keeps churning at FY2026's pace (AI-native CCaaS and the hyperscalers take the renewals), acquisitions are still made but no longer offset the decay, restructuring only holds the margin at 22% as fixed costs delever and lease costs rise as a share of a smaller base. Revenue is ~25% lower by FY2035 and still shrinking; terminal growth 0%, cap 12x. Not a solvency scenario -- the balance sheet is debt-free and FCF stays positive throughout.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 -6.0% is the nine-month actual (-6.0%, $352.0m vs $374.4m) carried through Q4 with no demand improvement, per management. FY2027 -3% and FY2028 -1%: Sixbell lapped, organic churn (Lifesize and legacy on-premise bases) still running -4% to -5% but partly offset by ~$30m/yr of tuck-ins; stabilises FY2029 and settles at 2% (nominal, mostly bought) from FY2032. The ten-year revenue CAGR is 0%: this is a no-growth base, not a return to the FY2013-2020 acquisition-compounder record.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC, post-IFRS-16, after restructuring charges. FY2025 was 24.8%; FY2026 23.5% absorbs the $4.6m Q3 FY2026 charge and revenue deleverage against management's 'mid-20s' adjusted guidance (which is before special charges); the $2-2.5m/quarter restructuring saving lifts it back to 25.0% by FY2029 and it stays there -- management said on the Q3 FY2026 call that high-20s is not coming back.
base.capex_rationale: 0.35% PP&E plus ~6% of revenue of acquisition spend ($28-30m/yr, the FY2025 pace of $33.4m scaled to the smaller base). This is the cash cost of the growth in the revenue path.
base.da_rationale: 6.3% in FY2026 (Sixbell intangibles added to a $29.5m amortisation run-rate that fell from $40.5m in FY2024) gliding to 4.0%: the remaining Vidyo/Dialogic/Lifesize intangibles finish amortising and ~$18m/yr of amortisation on ongoing deal flow plus ~$2.5m depreciation is the steady state.
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 14x (structurally slower business per the method's 12-15x guidance for low-growth names); Gordon at 2%/8.5% would be 16.2x, so the cap binds. Terminal growth 2.0% is nominal and funded by the 6.3% acquisition capex inside the terminal FCF.
base.wc_rationale: 20% capture on the CHANGE in revenue, all scenarios, anchored to the 2025-10-31 balance sheet: deferred revenue $115.1m (current 108.3 + non-current 6.8) plus accounts payable and accrued liabilities $76.2m less receivables $89.0m = net operating liabilities of ~$102m, ~20% of FY2025 revenue (ENGH.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:1497-1520). Positive sign because maintenance/SaaS is billed in advance; it means the shrinking FY2026-28 revenue in base and bear CONSUMES cash as deferred revenue unwinds (~-$6m in FY2026 base), and bull growth releases it.

bull.rationale: Demand stabilises in FY2027 and the 'buyer of last resort' thesis works: ~$35m/yr (7.5% of revenue) deployed into cheap software assets buys 3-3.5% net growth, restructuring and mix lift the margin to 27% (still below the 28-30% of FY2023-24), AMG transit/telecom keeps growing. Cap 15x, terminal 2.5%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: the organic decline is observed, not hypothetical (constant-currency revenue down in FY2025 and -6% reported for nine months of FY2026, recurring revenue itself falling), management says no near-term demand improvement, and the bear path is a continuation of the current run-rate rather than a new shock. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things (demand stabilisation, margin recovery to 27%, and a step-up in accretive M&A) to happen together; the base case already gives credit for continued acquisitions. No going-concern element in any scenario -- the company is debt-free with ~$270m of cash.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
